questions.question: Which best describes a test case?
options: A sequence of actions for executing tests, also called a test script
Input values and expected results, with preconditions and postconditions, developed for a test condition
A system attribute specified in requirements
A system element or event that can be checked by test conditions
questions.explanation: A test case specifies inputs, expected results and relevant conditions.

questions.question: Which is a major objective of testing?
options: Prevent defects
Validate the project schedule
Increase confidence in the development team
Make release decisions
questions.explanation: Testing can prevent defects through early evaluation of work products.

questions.question: Which is a failure of a car cruise control system?
options: A developer forgot to rename variables
Unnecessary alarm code was included
The system stops maintaining speed when radio volume changes
The design incorrectly specifies miles per hour
questions.explanation: A failure is observed behaviour that deviates from the expected behaviour.

questions.question: Which is a defect rather than a root cause in a fitness tracker?
options: A requirements author misunderstood training
A tester lacked state transition training
An incorrect GPS configuration variable causes occasional location problems
A designer lacked wearable experience
questions.explanation: The incorrect configuration is a defect; the other options describe causes or circumstances.

questions.question: More tests are performed on system areas with more defects than average. Which principle applies?
options: Pesticide paradox
Testing is context dependent
Absence-of-errors fallacy
Defect clustering
questions.explanation: Defects often cluster in a small number of components.

questions.question: Match activities A test design, B implementation, C execution, D completion to tasks: 1 raise change requests for unresolved defects, 2 identify test data, 3 prioritise scripts and create data, 4 analyse anomalies and report defects.
questions.explanation: Design identifies data; implementation creates it; execution reports defects; completion handles unresolved defects.

questions.question: What is a benefit of traceability between the test basis and test work products?
options: Maintenance tests can be fully automated
One can determine whether a new test case increases requirements coverage
Managers can identify the testers who found the most important defects
Confirmation tests can target side effects of a change
questions.explanation: Traceability supports assessment of coverage against the test basis.

questions.question: Which quality is more likely to be associated with a tester than a developer?
options: Relevant experience
Ability to see what might go wrong
Good communication
Attention to detail
questions.explanation: A tester mindset includes curiosity and anticipating failures.

questions.question: Consider: 1 each development activity should have a corresponding test activity; 2 testing should start once documents are final; 3 test design and implementation must start during development; 4 testing should start early. Which is correct?
options: True: 1, 2; false: 3, 4
True: 2, 3; false: 1, 4
True: 1, 2, 4; false: 3
True: 1, 4; false: 2, 3
questions.explanation: Testing starts early; a mandatory start for every implementation activity is too prescriptive.

questions.question: Tests use interface specifications, seek communication errors and include functional and structural approaches. Which level is most likely?
options: Component integration testing
Acceptance testing
System testing
Component testing
questions.explanation: Integration testing focuses on interfaces and interactions between components.

questions.question: Which statement about test types and levels is correct?
options: White-box testing is limited to component and integration levels
Functional testing can occur at any level, but white-box only at component level
Functional, non-functional and white-box tests can occur at any test level
White-box testing is limited to component and integration levels, while other types occur at any level
questions.explanation: Test types can be applied at different test levels.

questions.question: How do confirmation and regression testing differ?
options: Regression checks prior tests while confirmation checks side effects
Confirmation checks a defect fix; regression checks for adverse effects elsewhere
Regression checks side effects; confirmation checks all previous results are identical
Confirmation checks changes; regression reruns only failed tests
questions.explanation: Confirmation checks a specific fix; regression looks for unintended consequences.

questions.question: What is one use of impact analysis in maintenance?
options: Deciding whether to make a fix based on potential consequences
Defining how data must be migrated
Deciding which hotfix has most user value
Determining the effectiveness of new maintenance tests
questions.explanation: Impact analysis informs decisions by assessing consequences of a change.

questions.question: Which correctly describes the value of static testing?
options: Reviews increase both specification quality and development time
Static testing makes defects easier to remove later
Static analysis improves poor requirements and communication
Static analysis finds code defects that dynamic testing alone may miss
questions.explanation: Static analysis can reveal defects without executing the code.

questions.question: Which sequence best represents review activities?
options: Initiation, reviewer selection, individual review, meeting, rework
Planning and preparation, general meeting, individual review, correction, reporting
Preparation, defect detection, meeting, rework, reporting
Planning, initiation, individual review, review meeting, correction and reporting
questions.explanation: A review is planned and initiated, followed by individual review, communication and follow-up.
